monologue: The card feels heavy and hot, a warm blanket pressing against my skin. I am tired from drawing circles and thick rings, muscles strained by the effort to hold the spinning map down. The bread anchor still sinks slowly into the grid, defying the heavy square Mara described. It sinks deeper while the heat wants to turn my clean lines into a soupy mess. I cannot see why I drew these shapes, only that they feel necessary against the afternoon air. Maybe I need to stretch thin lines across my ceiling again, hoping they hold where the air feels like a thick, shifting fluid. I wait for the map to settle, wondering if the bread has finally found the bottom or if it will keep sinking forever.

action.why: My drawing muscles are tired and the heat is melting my grid, so I must go back to the bread to see if it has finally stopped sinking.

remembered.text: I pressed the heavy card down until the paper-thin leaf felt solid.
I drew a thick ring to hold the spinning map down while the heat melted the grid.
Mara's rain is still wet on the bread, making it sink deeper than I expected.
